nodes.name: ofc_analog.py

nodes.name: OFCAnalog

nodes.name: __init__

nodes.name: update

nodes.name: dacc.py

nodes.name: DACCConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen-form dataclass carrying all sub-weights, precision/effort constants, MECH-268 saturation knobs, SD-034 pe_cap hook, and SD-057 L7 goal-readout controls for the dACC adaptive-control cluster; every knob defaults to zero/false so the module is no-op unless explicitly activated via REEConfig.use_dacc.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl
nodes.summary: Stateful non-trainable dACC/aMCC-analog module that integrates precision-weighted affective PE (MECH-258), Shenhav EVC per-candidate expected value, Croxson reward-x-effort interaction, Kolling foraging value, MECH-260 recency suppression, MECH-268 outcome-history saturation, and Scholl 2017 drive-gated coupling into a per-tick control-plane bundle.

nodes.name: DACCtoE3Adapter
nodes.summary: Stopgap adapter converting a DACCAdaptiveControl integration bundle into an additive per-candidate E3 score bias with an absolute clamp and an independent SD-057 L7 (MECH-348) object-discriminative goal-readout term; to be removed once SD-032a salience-network coordinator lands.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl.__init__
nodes.summary: Initialises the dACC module's per-episode state: PE EMA slot, action-history ring for MECH-260, outcome-history FIFO for MECH-268 saturation, and per-tick diagnostic slots used by experiment scripts.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl._affective_pe
nodes.summary: MECH-258 precision-weighted affective prediction error pipeline: forms ||z_harm_a - z_harm_a_pred||, applies precision-normalised gain, clamps to SD-034 dacc_pe_cap, then attenuates by the MECH-268 history-conditioned saturation factor for the current outcome class.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl._saturation_factor
nodes.summary: MECH-268 f_sat computation: counts recurrences of the current outcome class within the recent outcome-history window and returns a habituation multiplier plus the recurrence count, returning 1.0 when saturation is disabled or the class cannot be determined.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl.record_outcome
nodes.summary: Pushes an outcome class onto the MECH-268 saturation FIFO with a bounded double-window buffer; ClosureOperator clears this on rule-completion firing.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl._suppression_penalty
nodes.summary: MECH-260 per-candidate recency penalty: fraction of the recent action-history ring occupied by the queried action class, used to suppress monostrategy re-selection.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl.inject_nogo
nodes.summary: SD-034 targeted No-Go: injects a completed action class into the MECH-260 recency ring multiple times to bias the striatum away from re-selection, clipped by history memory.

nodes.name: DACCAdaptiveControl.forward
nodes.summary: Core per-tick dACC integration: computes precision-weighted PE, Shenhav EVC mode_ev, Croxson reward-x-effort interaction, choice difficulty, MECH-260 per-candidate suppression penalties, Kolling foraging value, SD-049 per-axis drive-gated coupling, and packages the full control-plane bundle including SD-057 L7 goal-readout and MECH-268 saturation diagnostics.

nodes.name: DACCtoE3Adapter.forward
nodes.summary: Converts a DACCAdaptiveControl bundle into a per-candidate E3 score bias by combining -mode_ev, Croxson interaction, Kolling foraging, and MECH-260 suppression terms with drive-gated dacc_weight and an absolute clamp, then adds an independently-weighted SD-057 L7 goal-readout term after the clamp so goal-conditioned bias survives even when the legacy dACC path is off.

nodes.name: goal.py

nodes.name: GoalConfig

nodes.name: IncentiveTokenBank

nodes.name: GoalState
nodes.summary: Persistent z_goal attractor with EMA update, drive-gated seeding threshold, SD-092 hierarchical parent-goal credit, SD-093 progress-velocity effort modulation, and MECH-188 injection view for scoring.

nodes.name: serotonin.py

nodes.name: SerotoninConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass for SerotoninModule dynamics: baseline, benefit sensitivity, harm suppression, decay rate, phase-specific factors, plus SR-2/SR-3 gains and MECH-204 REM recalibration knobs.

nodes.name: SerotoninModule
nodes.summary: Tonic-5HT scalar state machine with per-phase step dynamics, benefit/harm salience tags (SR-2), REM zero-point capture (SR-3), and MECH-204 target precision recalibration.

nodes.name: structured_curiosity.py
nodes.summary: Pure-arithmetic MECH-314 structured curiosity bonus regulator combining novelty (314a), uncertainty (314b), and learning-progress (314c) sub-flavors into a per-candidate E3 score bias with auto-augmentation streak tracking.
nodes.languageNotes: Sibling-pattern regulator (no nn.Module, no learned params) exposing three independently-togglable sub-flavours for Q-044 ablation; MECH-094 simulation-mode gated.

nodes.name: StructuredCuriosityConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding MECH-314 curiosity master switch, three sub-flavour flags, per-flavour weights, clamp scale, LP EMA/window parameters, and Phase-2 novelty auto-augmentation controls.

nodes.name: StructuredCuriosity
nodes.summary: Pure-arithmetic curiosity regulator that composes MECH-314a novelty, MECH-314b uncertainty, and MECH-314c learning-progress into a clamped per-candidate score bias, honoring MECH-094 simulation-mode gating and tracking auto-augmentation streaks.
nodes.languageNotes: Non-nn.Module regulator with three orthogonally-toggleable channels; state is scalars/ring buffers only; broadcast Phase-1 for 314b/c with per-candidate 314a.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Validates all StructuredCuriosityConfig sub-flags, weights, gains, thresholds, and window sizes; raises ValueError on any invalid setting before initializing counters and LP ring buffer.

nodes.name: compute_score_bias
nodes.summary: Main per-tick entry point that dispatches to Phase-2 novelty when enabled, composes weighted MECH-314a/b/c contributions into a K-length bias vector, clamps to +/-bias_scale, and records diagnostic ranges and rail hits.

nodes.name: _compute_novelty_phase2
nodes.summary: Phase-2 novelty computation that consumes coerced RBF centers, monitors candidate spread against the min-spread threshold, updates auto-augmentation streaks, and toggles first-action one-hot augmentation when the streak triggers.

nodes.name: _candidate_spread
nodes.summary: Computes mean pairwise L2 distance across K candidate summaries under no_grad as a scalar spread diagnostic feeding the auto-augmentation streak controller.

nodes.name: _update_augmentation_streak
nodes.summary: Advances or resets the consecutive-low-spread streak counter, flipping first-action one-hot augmentation on when the streak crosses the configured tick threshold.

nodes.name: _coerce_source_to_centers
nodes.summary: Normalizes heterogeneous novelty-source inputs (lists, tensors, arrays) into a detached [N,D] tensor on the target device for Phase-2 novelty processing.

nodes.name: _compute_novelty
nodes.summary: MECH-314a per-candidate novelty via minimum distance from each candidate's first-step z_world to the nearest active RBF center, optionally augmented with first-action one-hots, normalized by mean signature norm.

nodes.name: _compute_uncertainty
nodes.summary: MECH-314b uncertainty scalar read from E3 running variance, broadcast in Phase-1 across candidates and normalized to a nonnegative float.

nodes.name: update_prediction_error
nodes.summary: Feeds a per-tick prediction-error scalar into the MECH-314c learning-progress ring buffer and refreshes the LP EMA of |PE_t - PE_{t-K}|, gated by simulation_mode to protect replay paths.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears LP ring buffer, EMA state, augmentation streak/state, and per-tick diagnostic counters on episode reset.

nodes.name: get_state
nodes.summary: Returns a diagnostic dict of curiosity state including LP buffer size, EMA value, augmentation streak, and per-flavour contribution ranges for downstream logging and Q-044 ablation checks.

nodes.name: OPERATOR_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive operator guide for the Phase 3 coordinator/sync_daemon shadow-coordination system, covering the Explorer coordination panel, three-system architecture (git, coordinator API, sync_daemon writers), five-phase cutover, troubleshooting, hub telemetry transport, and daemon/config drift diagnostics.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive operator runbook with detailed troubleshooting for hub-writer wedge, daemon code drift, and unit config drift incidents; heavy cross-references to shadow.conf templates, service unit files, and phase3 environment gates.

nodes.name: manifest_spool.py
nodes.summary: Filesystem spool that lets the /result HTTP endpoint persist raw manifest bytes and companion sidefiles keyed on run_id, so the Phase 3 sole-git-writer in sync_daemon.py can later commit them into REE_assembly without touching git from the runner. Every write is atomic-rename with sha256 verification and gated on the COORDINATOR_SPOOL_DIR environment flag; layout is <spool>/pending/<run_id>.json plus <spool>/sidefiles/pending/<run_id>/<relpath>.
nodes.languageNotes: Filesystem-level path safety: every path is verified via resolve().relative_to(root) before touching disk, defending against traversal via crafted run_ids or manifest_relpaths from POST payloads.

nodes.name: spool_root
nodes.summary: Returns the configured COORDINATOR_SPOOL_DIR as a Path, or None when the env var is unset — the master feature switch for all spool writes.

nodes.name: write_manifest
nodes.summary: Atomically writes a manifest and its metadata sidecar for a given run_id: rejects unsafe run_ids, hashes-and-verifies incoming bytes, uses tmp-then-rename with fsync so a crash never leaves a half-file for the writer to consume.

nodes.name: count_pending
nodes.summary: Counts .json files currently sitting in the pending manifest directory — a health-check hook the coordinator exposes to detect backpressure.

nodes.name: list_pending_run_ids
nodes.summary: Enumerates run_ids with pending manifests, deduplicated by pairing .json and .meta.json files, so the writer can process each run atomically.

nodes.name: read_manifest
nodes.summary: Reads the raw manifest bytes for a pending run_id, returning None if either the run_id is unsafe or the file is missing (a caller may have already consumed it).

nodes.name: read_meta
nodes.summary: Reads the JSON metadata sidecar (received_at, sha, optional manifest_relpath hint) accompanying a pending manifest.

nodes.name: delete_manifest
nodes.summary: Removes the manifest and its metadata sidecar after a successful writer commit; tolerates missing files so partial-crash recovery is idempotent.

nodes.name: derive_evidence_relpath
nodes.summary: Resolves where in REE_assembly a manifest should land: prefers the runner-supplied manifest_relpath (validated safe), otherwise falls back to evidence/experiments/<run_id>.json to match the legacy flat layout.

nodes.name: safe_companion_relpath
nodes.summary: Validates a sidefile relative path against traversal and absolute-path attacks before it is used as a filesystem key inside the sidefile spool.

nodes.name: write_sidefile
nodes.summary: Spools a companion sidefile under <spool>/sidefiles/pending/<run_id>/<relpath> using tmp-then-rename with sha256 verification, so the writer can later either commit it alongside its manifest or quarantine it under the oversized threshold.

nodes.name: list_pending_sidefile_run_ids
nodes.summary: Enumerates run_ids that currently have queued sidefiles, so the writer can pair them with their manifest at commit time.

nodes.name: list_sidefiles_for_run
nodes.summary: Recursively lists every sidefile currently spooled for a given run_id along with its safe companion relpath, filtering out any traversal-unsafe entries a partial crash may have left behind.

nodes.name: delete_sidefiles
nodes.summary: Removes every sidefile and metadata for a run and cleans up empty parent directories, called by the writer after a successful commit of the run's sidefile set.

nodes.name: placemarker_relpath_for
nodes.summary: Returns the deterministic relpath under which an oversized-sidefile placemarker is stored — a small JSON stub that lives in git while the real payload sits in cloud storage.

nodes.name: sha256_of_file
nodes.summary: Streams a file through hashlib.sha256 in 1MB chunks to compute a stable content hash without loading the whole payload — used both to verify writes and to fingerprint oversized sidefiles in placemarkers.

nodes.name: build_oversized_sidefile_placemarker
nodes.summary: Constructs the JSON body of an oversized-sidefile placemarker recording the sha, size, oversized threshold, external storage locations, and a note explaining that the real bytes were quarantined off-git.

nodes.name: theta_buffer.py
nodes.summary: ThetaBuffer implements cross-rate integration for MECH-089/SD-006, giving E3 temporally-averaged theta-cycle summaries of z_world/z_self instead of raw per-tick E1/E2 output. Supports SD-100 phase-weighted summaries and MECH-122 consolidation-mode packaging.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure PyTorch scalar/tensor arithmetic, no nn.Module; uses collections.deque as the rolling backing store.

nodes.name: ThetaBuffer
nodes.summary: Rolling theta-cycle buffer that tracks recent z_world/z_self estimates from E1 and produces theta-cycle summaries (flat mean, phase-weighted, or consolidation-mode packaging) consumed by E3 at heartbeat ticks.

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: salience_coordinator.py
nodes.summary: SD-032a salience-network coordinator: aggregates dACC bundle plus homeostatic/offline signals into a soft operating-mode probability vector with Schmitt-trigger hysteresis, MECH-259 mode-switch trigger, and the MECH-261 dict-keyed write-gate registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic regulator (no nn.Module, no learned parameters); non-trainable dataclass-config module with softmax mode-probability computation, MECH-266 asymmetric per-mode enter/exit thresholds, and MECH-048 mu/kappa temperature overlays.

nodes.name: SalienceCoordinatorConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding SalienceCoordinator tunables: mode affinity weights, external-task bias, softmax temperature, MECH-048 stability-temperature overlays, MECH-266 per-mode enter/exit hysteresis thresholds, salience-signal weights, and affinity input cap.

nodes.name: SalienceCoordinator
nodes.summary: Network-level coordinator that ticks the mode-probability softmax, applies Schmitt-trigger hysteresis (MECH-266) to derive current_mode, exposes mode-conditioned write_gate values (MECH-261 registry), and emits switch triggers when salience aggregate crosses per-mode enter thresholds while current mode falls below its exit rail.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: Core per-cycle update: consumes dACC bundle plus registered signals, folds SD-057 per-axis-drive into external-task affinity, computes mode-probability softmax with MECH-048 mu/kappa effective-temperature overlays, and applies MECH-266 asymmetric enter/exit rails to fire mode-switch triggers.

nodes.name: field.py
nodes.summary: Residue field: RBF-layer-backed distributed representation of residual salience/care markers consumed by hippocampal and predictor modules.

nodes.name: RBFLayer
nodes.summary: Radial basis function layer used inside the residue field to embed and read out spatial/latent residues.

nodes.name: ResidueField
nodes.summary: Residue field: distributed store of residual signals (care markers, mood, salience) built on RBFLayer, read by the hippocampal module and the E3 selector.

nodes.name: mel_consumer.py
nodes.summary: SD-MEL-CONSUMER (sleep_substrate GAP-5b) adaptive sleep-cadence controller that reads accumulated waking Model Error Load (MEL) and modulates SWS/REM sleep-phase duration and entry timing. Implements INV-050's learning-demand sleep drive as a pure-arithmetic regulator over the SD-017 sleep cycle.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic dataclass-based regulator, no torch/nn.Module dependencies, single-module implementation of a load-bearing V3 substrate.

nodes.name: MELConsumerConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass configuration for the MEL consumer, mirrored on REEConfig. Holds knobs for gain, reference-tracking mode, duration-factor bounds, per-phase scaling, and entry-timing threshold.

nodes.name: WakingMELAccumulator
nodes.summary: Streaming accumulator for per-step E3 prediction error magnitudes across a waking window. Filters non-finite inputs and exposes running mean/count with reset semantics.

nodes.name: MELConsumer
nodes.summary: Adaptive sleep-cadence regulator: accumulates waking MEL, tracks an EMA/fixed reference, computes a clamped duration factor scaling SWS/REM passes, and gates entry via a relative-novelty threshold. Emits diagnostics for cadence attribution.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic; relative-response design (mel/ref, never absolute) with a small floor to guard div-by-zero; MECH-094 gated at caller.

nodes.name: phase_manager.py
nodes.summary: SleepLoopManager: deterministic K-episode driver for the SD-017 sleep cycle plus the sleep_substrate GAP-9 within-life step trigger. Composes the Phase B-E consumers (replay sampler, routing gate, Bayesian aggregator, self-model aggregator, MEL consumer, cross-module consolidator) into a single cycle orchestrator.
nodes.languageNotes: Long orchestrator class (~700 lines) with heavy conditional wiring of optional Phase B-E consumers; welfare_relevant marker denotes offline harm-content resampling.

nodes.name: SleepPhase
nodes.summary: Enum of canonical sleep-cycle phases (WAKING, SLEEP_ENTRY, SWS_ANALOG, PHASE_SWITCH, REM_ANALOG, WRITEBACK). Reserves intermediate tokens for Phase D aggregator and Phase E writeback.

nodes.name: SleepCycleState
nodes.summary: Per-cycle bookkeeping dataclass: cycle index, current phase, episodes/steps since last sleep, and last-cycle metrics. Reset at the start of each sleep cycle.

nodes.name: SleepLoopManager
nodes.summary: Central sleep-cycle driver: increments per-episode/per-step counters, fires the SD-017 cycle via K-episode cadence, MEL entry-timing, or within-life step ceiling, and orchestrates Phase B-E consumers (replay sampler, routing gate, Bayesian aggregators, MEL consumer, cross-module consolidator, MECH-204 precision writeback).
nodes.languageNotes: The `_run_cycle` method is the load-bearing method (~350 lines) composing every optional Phase B-E consumer, extract-region tagging, evidence lookup, and MECH-204 precision recalibration.

nodes.name: _run_cycle
nodes.summary: Core sleep-cycle orchestrator: gates on SD-017 substrate presence and MECH-286 sleep-onset permit, drives SWS then REM passes through the replay sampler / routing gate / Bayesian + self-model aggregators, applies MECH-204 precision recalibration + MECH-273 partial staleness decay, and merges per-cycle metrics.

nodes.name: notify_waking_step
nodes.summary: sleep_substrate GAP-9 within-life sleep trigger. Called once per waking step from REEAgent.update_residue; fires a sleep cycle when accumulated MEL crosses the entry threshold (design (b) primary) or the within-life step ceiling is hit (design (a) backstop). Records arm-attribution diagnostics.

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: phase3_verify.py

nodes.name: _classify_commits

nodes.name: check_sync_daemon_phase3_tick

nodes.name: check_workers_no_result_git_push

nodes.name: CausalGridWorld

nodes.summary: Resolves the ARC-071 policy-chunking deliberation horizon from REEConfig (sentinel 0 mirrors HippocampalConfig.horizon, positive values override) so both the size and depth growable-ceiling knobs read one shared budget without silent misconfiguration.

nodes.summary: Lightweight dataclass carrying per-tick agent state (latent tensors, phase counters, mode flags) for use by consumers that need a serialisable snapshot without importing the full REEAgent class.

nodes.name: REEAgent
nodes.summary: The central V3 agent class integrating every REE substrate (latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal proposer, residue field, MECH-090 beta-gate, MECH-279 PAG, cingulate cluster, PFC subdivisions, amygdala, sleep loop, defensive-orienting and hazard-avoidance gates, policy chunking/decomposition, coalition controller). Exposes act/sense/select_action/update_residue as the public API and orchestrates the multi-rate SENSE->E1->E2->E3->SELECT->ACT->RESIDUE loop with offline replay, SWS/REM sleep passes, and dozens of flag-gated wiring points for the substrate design decisions documented in CLAUDE.md.
nodes.languageNotes: 95 methods spanning ~11500 lines. Nearly every substrate flag introduced across the REE build history is wired here via getattr-fallback so a default-off configuration remains bit-identical.

Core predictive-coding substrate feeding E3 selection and downstream consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive use of torch.nn.Module subclasses with register_buffer for non-parameter state; heavy config-driven gating via getattr fallbacks.

nodes.name: ContextMemory
nodes.summary: Slot-based attention memory with configurable write-address selection (argmin/refractory) and optional usage-balancing conscience bias. Repairs the write-path addressing degeneracy where a near-constant query stream locks writes into a single slot.

nodes.name: E1DeepPredictor
nodes.summary: Long-horizon E1 world predictor: LSTM transition model with ContextMemory read/write, schema salience readout (MECH-216), SD-016 cue-slot tagging for frontal cue-indexed integration, and multiple auxiliary training losses (attention entropy, context divergence, schema readout).

nodes.summary: Reads from memory via query-key attention: bmm(query, keys) -> softmax weights -> weighted sum of values -> output projection.

nodes.summary: Writes to memory: computes write gate and content, selects a target slot via configured selection rule, and blends. Runs under no_grad; updates usage EMA and recent-write ring buffer for refractory/conscience modes.

nodes.summary: Selects the target slot index for a write, honoring refractory windows and usage-balancing bias when enabled; falls back to argmin over selection_scores otherwise.

nodes.summary: SD-016 Path 1: mean squared off-diagonal cosine similarity between normalized slots, used as an auxiliary diversification loss to break slot-collapse.

tour.title: Central Agent Entry Point
tour.description: REEAgent is the ~11,500-line god-class that composes every V3 substrate: the latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal module, residue field, cingulate cluster, PFC subdivisions, amygdala, goals, regulators, and sleep. Reading this file first tells you which subsystems exist and how they wire together at the top level. Almost every later step in the tour zooms into a cluster this file imports.
tour.languageLesson: The 'god-class as integration point' pattern is common in research substrates where each experiment needs a full-stack agent; downside is that 95 methods live in one file, so grep the file rather than trying to browse it linearly.

tour.title: Configuration Surface
tour.description: Every substrate cluster the agent composes is parameterised through a dataclass config declared here (latent stack, E1/E2/E3, event segmenter, invalidation trigger, anchor set, ghost-goal bank, hippocampal, residue field, heartbeat, environment, and more). Reading this file gives you the vocabulary of knobs experiments are allowed to twist; anything not exposed here is either hardcoded or a bug.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses centralise defaults and type hints for a large configuration surface; `from_dims()`-style factory classmethods build sub-configs from a shared dimension spec. Note the 'silent kwargs' hazard called out in project memory: adding a new field means updating the dataclass, `from_dims`, and every construction site.

tour.title: The Latent Space (z_self / z_world)
tour.description: SD-005 splits the latent space into z_self and z_world encoders, with dedicated harm-stream encoders (SD-010/SD-011), a reafference predictor (SD-007), harm forward models (ARC-033/ARC-058) and an adversarial split head. This is the representational substrate everything downstream (predictors, hippocampal, residue) operates on, so getting the split right is a prerequisite to interpreting any experiment result.

tour.title: Predictors: E2 Fast Forward, E3 Trajectory Selector
tour.description: E2 is the fast self/world forward-model pair used for counterfactual rollouts and candidate generation. E3 scores hippocampal trajectory candidates on terrain, harm, benefit, goal and modulatory biases, and arbitrates commit-vs-deliberate through dynamic precision (including ARC-107 basal-ganglia-style gating). Together they answer 'what will happen if I try each option?' and 'which do I actually commit to?'

tour.title: Residue Field: the Care Marker
tour.description: The residue field is an RBF-backed distributed store of care markers, load-bearing for the ethical-agency thesis the substrate exists to test (residue-as-care-marker distinguishes real care from simulation). It is read by the hippocampal module and both predictor stacks, which is why it ranks high in fan-in despite being a small file.

tour.title: Hippocampal Cluster: Trajectory Proposal, Anchors, Ghost Goals
tour.description: The hippocampal module navigates the SD-004 action-object space and generates value-flat CEM trajectory proposals under ARC-007 STRICT. It sits atop a scale-tagged anchor set (MECH-269), a MECH-292 ghost-goal ranking view over those anchors, and a per-anchor staleness accumulator that integrates and leaks over time. These four files are tightly coupled and are best read together as a pipeline: anchors go in, staleness updates them, the ghost-goal bank ranks them, and the module consumes the ranking to steer proposals.

tour.title: Goals and Attractors
tour.description: z_goal is a slow-decay attractor living in z_world space (introduced in Step 3), plus an incentive-salience token bank (SD-057) and a super-ordinal cross-episode goal-anchor store (MECH-189). This is what makes the agent 'want' something across time; the hippocampal and predictor clusters from Steps 4-6 all read from it.

tour.title: Cortical Control: PFC, Cingulate, Policy, Regulators
tour.description: The four cluster barrels wire the top-level control substrates the agent uses to modulate the predictor/hippocampal core. PFC re-exports the escape-affordance linker/bridge plus frontopolar, lateral-PFC, OFC, and a trainable escape learner. Cingulate re-exports the SD-032 dACC/AIC/pACC/PCC salience coordinator and stuck-state detector. Policy re-exports gated/candidate-rule/curiosity/vigor/noise-floor/commit-maintenance regulators. Regulators re-exports SD-036 GABAergic decay, MECH-287 invalidation trigger, SD-037 broadcast override, SD-069 phasic surprise burst, and the MECH-282 LPB interoceptive channel.
tour.languageLesson: Python 'barrel' packages (`__init__.py` doing re-exports) let a large subsystem present a small public surface. Grep-for-symbol falls through to the barrel first, then to the concrete module; reading the barrel first is often the fastest way to see what a cluster contains.

tour.title: Sleep Cluster: Phases B/C/D/E
tour.description: The sleep loop is a deterministic K-episode driver (Phase A) that composes four consumers: a MECH-272 routing gate (Phase C) that channel-weights replay events, a MECH-275 Bayesian aggregator (Phase D) that maintains per-domain per-region Gaussian posteriors over residuals, and a MECH-273 self-model aggregator (Phase E) that runs bounded low-LR offline passes on the SD-003 causal_sig posterior. This cluster is where offline consolidation of the care-markers from Step 5 and the goal state from Step 7 actually happens.

tour.title: Coordinator: Plan-of-Record and Operator Guide
tour.description: Having toured the substrate, we pivot to the harness that runs experiments against it. PLAN.md defines the coordinator's rationale, target end-state architecture, HTTP API contract, SQLite schema, and phased/reversible rollout. OPERATOR_GUIDE.md then walks the day-to-day view: the Explorer coordination panel, the three-system architecture (git, coordinator API, sync_daemon writers), and the five-phase cutover. Read PLAN first for the design, OPERATOR_GUIDE for how it looks in practice.

tour.title: Coordinator Runtime: HTTP Service and SQLite Layer
tour.description: app.py is a ThreadingHTTPServer exposing bearer-authenticated GET/POST endpoints for claim arbitration, heartbeats, result manifest ingestion, and command dispatch. db.py is its SQLite persistence layer, handling schema migrations, claim arbitration (with the departure-based reaper), heartbeat/status recording, shutdown-notice bookkeeping, and command dispatch. db.py has the highest fan-in in the whole graph (14) because every coordinator endpoint routes through it.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The six-table SQLite schema is the ground truth for everything the coordinator does. The `experiments` table tracks queue lifecycle (pending -> claimed -> running -> completed) and is what backs the git queue snapshot db.py from Step 11 arbitrates over. `results` stores the manifest bytes the /result endpoint ingests (referenced by run_id, with PASS/FAIL/ERROR classification). `heartbeats` is the per-machine liveness state that drives the Explorer dashboard, and `commands` is the pause/resume/stop/kick/release_claim channel workers poll.
tour.languageLesson: In SQLite, integer primary keys are aliases for ROWID; append-only log tables (like the sibling heartbeat_log / claim_log) trade write cost for a full audit trail, which is why the coordinator can reconstruct the fleet's history without a separate event bus.

tour.title: Sync Daemon and Manifest Spool: DB back into Git
tour.description: The coordinator is the sole authority for coordination data at runtime, but the project's ground truth lives in git. sync_daemon.py is the sole-writer daemon that materialises the DB from Step 12 into three git artifacts (result manifests, the experiment_queue snapshot, and runner heartbeats/status), with dirty-tree guards and rebase-conflict recovery. manifest_spool.py bridges the HTTP layer to the writer: /result persists raw manifest bytes to disk keyed on run_id, and sync_daemon later commits them. PHASE3_CUTOVER.md explains why the hub had to become sole writer in the first place.

tour.title: Preflight and Post-Cutover Verification
tour.description: The two verification scripts are how the operator gains confidence the Phase-3 architecture from Steps 10-13 is actually in the state it claims. phase3_preflight.py probes coordinator, DB, and sync-daemon over SSH and HTTP, resolving a pre/mid/post-cutover verdict with advisory and blocking status per subsystem. phase3_verify.py runs the battery of post-cutover assertions: sync_daemon really is the sole git writer for coordination artifacts, workers no longer push, telemetry really is derived from the DB, and no foreign commits crept in. Together they close the loop: substrate (Steps 1-9) runs, coordinator (Steps 10-13) captures results, and verify proves the capture is honest.
